To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nucleotide sequence of the ermAM determinant is highly homologous to that of the erythromy-cin-resistant plasmid pA77 and transposon T917.
the erm determinant of the S. faecalis plas- mid pAM beta 2 is 5' truncated, and that this deletion is responsible for the constitutive ex- pression of the erm determinant of pAM beta 3.
the erm gene is present in a variety of gram-positive bacteria and that it confers resistance to the macrolide-lincosamide-streptogramin B group of antibiotics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of erythromycine resistance.
the molecular biology of the erythromycincin resistance determinant of the plasmid pAMBeta1.
the characterization of the erm determinant of pAM beta 16 and with the analysis of the regulatory region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ermAM is an erythromycin-resistance determinant of the Tn917 family, which has lost its regulatory sequences.
ermAM of pAM beta 11 is a deletion derivative of ermAM of pAD1 and Tn917, and that the ermAM of pC194 and Tn917 is a deletion derivative from ermAM of pE194 and pAM beta 3, respectively.
pAM beta 16 is a derivative of pAM beta 2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pAM beta 2 and pAM beta 3, the two plasmid derivatives of pAM beta 4, have a similar erythromycin-resistant phenotype.
ermAM is a member of the ermB family of determinants.
pAM beta 15 is a derivative of pAM beta 3 and that pAM beta1, pAM77, and Tn917 are closely related.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the nucleotide sequence of the ermAM gene to design a new method for the detection of Streptococcus pyogenes.
